# Sensitive paths (docs/GOVERNANCE.md step 3).
#
# A path listed here may land on `main` directly only when pushed by an
# operator whose registry file (operators/<slug>.md) declares
# `sensitive_owner: true`. For anyone else the debrief routes it into a
# proposal pull request, the local pre-push hook (githooks/pre-push) refuses
# a direct push of it, and the CI tripwire
# (.github/workflows/sensitive-tripwire.yml) opens an issue if one reaches
# `main` anyway.
#
# Syntax, one entry per line:
#   pattern      shell glob matched against the whole repo-relative path;
#                `*` also matches `/`, so `areas/finance/*` covers every depth.
#   !pattern     exception: a path matching it is never sensitive, even if a
#                pattern would catch it. Exceptions win wherever they sit.
#   # comment    ignored, as are blank lines.
#
# The file ships inert: nothing below is active until you uncomment or add a
# line. Keep it a subset of the scopes you route to named reviewers in
# .github/CODEOWNERS; /system-checkup reports drift between the two. A path
# escapes the structural and sensitive classes only when every list whose
# patterns would catch it also exempts it, so an exception meant for both
# lists is written in both.
#
# !areas/finance/public-summary.md
# areas/finance/*
# areas/legal/*
#
# The registry is the root of trust for the whole recipe: whether a path may be
# pushed straight to `main` is read from operators/<slug>.md, so a change to
# that folder is a change to who may push what. Without the line below, an
# operator can grant themselves `sensitive_owner: true` in an ordinary commit.
# operators/*
